subject: turtle
pitch: A green sea turtle gliding through the water. A heart-shaped shell with olive and caramel plates traced in darker brown, a pale yellow belly plate, a blunt head with cream-edged scales, dark wise eyes and a gentle beak. Long front flippers spread wide, short rear flippers, and a little remora fish riding under its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for a green sea turtle model, roughly 1.1m shell length, facing +Z in a gliding pose with flippers spread, positioned at a height suggesting it's swimming through water rather than resting on ground.

I'm reviewing the set of builder APIs available — joints, chains, sweeps, parts, extrusions, lathes, and paint patterns — to plan how I'll construct the shell, flippers, and head using scales or countershading for texture, while keeping the eyes simple with sphere geometry instead of decals.

For the shell shape itself, I'm weighing options: a flattened sphere with scale distortion, an extruded heart outline, or a lathe profile, trying to capture the dome curvature plus the heart-like notch typical of a sea turtle shell as seen from above.

I think a loft is the cleanest approach — defining a series of stations along the body axis with varying width and height to approximate the heart shape, wide near the front shoulders, narrowing toward the tail, with elliptical cross-sections giving it the dome profile.

For the rest of the turtle, I'm planning a lower plastron as a flatter loft or scaled sphere in cream/yellow beneath the shell, then separate parts for the head, beak, dark eyes with tiny highlights, and front flippers built as joint chains with a flattened sweep profile tapering toward the tips.

For the flipper chains, I'm working out how many path points and names produce the right number of span joints plus a tip joint, mirroring left and right sides across X, and giving rear flippers a shorter three-point chain while the head gets its own neck joint.

Now I'm placing the actual skeleton coordinates: a root "hips" joint near the body center, a neck chain running from the shell front toward the head, and working out the shell's overall dimensions (length, width, top/bottom y) so the head, neck, and water line all sit in sensible proportion to each other.

I'm defining the shell loft stations, specifying width and height at each z-position along the body to shape the front, middle, and tail sections, including a subtle widening near the shoulders to suggest the classic heart-like front contour. I'm also assigning the loft to the hips bone and starting to set up the shell's scale coloring with olive and caramel tones.

For the belly plate, I'm positioning a smaller loft slightly below the shell's lower edge so it peeks out minimally from underneath, giving it a cream-yellow color to suggest the plastron.

For the head, I'm adding scale texture using an olive-green base with cream edges, plus dark eyes with a tiny highlight for a lifelike touch. The flippers get a simple dark olive color, possibly with a subtle edge treatment.

I'm also considering adding a small remora fish attached near the shell, built from an elongated body shape with a flat oval sucker disc on top of its head.

Setting the remora's size and position so it clears the shell bottom without touching the ground, then working out the orientation math for its sucker disc so the oval lies flat on top of its head using the extrude thickness direction.

Now I'm sketching the beak as a tapered capsule shape between the mouth and snout points, and setting up the head geometry as a scaled sphere with local coordinate helpers for placing eyes relative to the head's forward/up/left directions.

For the neck, I'm building a short catmull chain between the body front and head base with a tapering sweep radius, then attaching the head joint to the end of that chain with an aim direction pointing forward and slightly up.

For the head itself, I'm placing a scaled sphere slightly forward of the head joint using local offsets, then building a beak as a tapering capsule positioned forward and slightly down from the head, and considering splitting it into upper and lower jaw parts for a more lifelike mouth.

Now I'm setting up a jaw joint under the head with its own aim direction, then creating upper and lower beak capsules anchored to the head and jaw respectively, tapering from wider at the base to narrower at the tip. I'm adding small dark eye spheres with tiny cream highlight dots positioned on the sides of the head, then moving on to the front flippers, planning a shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip joint chain with the shoulder positioned on the body side and the elbow spread outward to give the flipper a natural splayed shape.

Writing flipper chain code...

Now for the rear flippers, I'm sketching a shorter path from hip to ankle to tip using a catmull-rom curve with a smaller sweep radius profile, plus a stubby tail chain extending back from the body with its own minimal sweep.

For paint, I'm layering scale patterns on the head, neck, and flippers using countershading between olive-green and cream tones, keeping the shell's darker plate pattern handled separately. For the remora attachment, I'm building its body as a sweep along a catmull-rom path running tight along the shell surface.

I'm checking vertical positioning so the remora doesn't clip through the plastron, shifting it down slightly and adding a small sucker disc on its head via a thin oval extrusion.

Now I'm sketching a tail fin for the remora, extruding a thin triangular outline at the back of its body using points offset along the z and y axes to form the fin shape.

I'm also thinking through the eye coloring—dark brown with a cream highlight for a wise look—and planning the code structure: which imports I'll need (builder, scales, countershading), how the shell loft will use station data with position, width, and height to interpolate the shell's curved surface.

For the shell texture itself, I'm applying an olive-and-caramel scale pattern over a dark brown base, then placing the head sphere slightly scaled and offset forward from a head joint, with a neck chain built from a few curved points connecting the body to the head.

Now I'm working out the hips root, shoulder joint placement near the shell edge for the flippers, and setting up the color palette — olive and caramel shell tones, a cream belly, dark eyes, a muted beak color, and darker remora tones for the hitchhiking fish detail.

Writing shell loft geometry... I'm shaping the carapace as a series of elliptical stations tapering from a wide front near the neck opening down to a narrow tail point, then adding a similar loft for the plastron underside with slightly smaller cross-sections.

I'm checking clearances between plastron, shell rim, and the remora attached below to make sure nothing clips awkwardly, accepting a bit of visible overlap as a natural rim effect. Now I'm defining the neck as a chain following a curved path up from the hips, then sweeping a tapered tube along it and planning to apply a scaled pattern in head-green tones for texture.

I'm placing the head as a joint at the end of the neck with an aim direction, then sizing a sphere for the skull and adjusting its forward offset so the beak and eyes sit correctly relative to the head's front edge, nudging the beak capsule and jaw joint positions outward so they protrude properly beyond the skull.

Still writing beak and eye geometry, then setting up the flipper chain with sweep radius tapering from shoulder to tip...

Now I'm working through the hind flipper chains, remora placement with its sucker and tail fin extrudes, and the turtle's tail stub capsule, making sure bone parenting and paint colors (dark shell, pale belly countershading) line up correctly on each part. I'm also double-checking type signatures for outline points and extrude thickness directions so everything orients properly in world space, then finalizing the root joint setup and exported metadata before assembling the complete code.
